definition.simple: A company swaps several old shares for one new share. You have fewer shares at a higher price, and your total value is unchanged on the day.
definition.balanced: In a 1-for-10 reverse split, every 10 shares become 1 and the price is multiplied by about 10. Nothing about the business changes. Companies sometimes do it to lift a falling share price above a level they need. Repeated reverse splits alongside repeated [[dilution]] are a warning sign worth investigating.

example: Fictional: 10,000 shares at 0.12 USD (1,200 USD) become 1,000 shares at 1.20 USD (still 1,200 USD).
